//: TODO(design): first batch of events, written by Claude for M5 (GAME_DESIGN.md §10, §14); texts and numbers are working values, change them freely. An event happens when the hydra steps on an event site on the map (balance.json undergroundGenerator.rings[].eventSites). Of the events that fit (conditions, as in dialogues.json), those with the highest priority are drawn by weight. once: happens at most once in a hydra's life (default true). A step of a mini quest also has notFlags with its own flags, so that a step done in an earlier generation doesn't come again (the quest's flags are world knowledge, flags.json). quest: the mini quest the event is a step of (steps are chained by flags: a step sets a flag, the next step needs it). A choice can need a head (needsHead: class id) or a condition on the hydra (needsCondition: world.json conditions, e.g. warmed), cost resources (cost), and either have one outcome, or be a gamble: chance (0–1) of success, otherwise failure. An outcome has a text and may: give or take muck, moisture, bones; change the alert; heal or hurt the body (bodyHp) and every head (headsHp, never below 1); put a condition on the hydra (condition, world.json); show the map around (reveal: hexes); start a battle (battle: an encounter group, enemies.json); set flags (setFlags); start a dialogue (dialogue: an id from dialogues.json); grow a head (newHead: class id); have the Cinderkin melt a tunnel through the rock nearby (bore: true; how, in world.json thresholds.cinderBore); give the hydra a mutation for her and her heiresses (mutation: an id from mutations.json).

events.title: A Novice with a Checklist
events.text: A novice of the Order of the Eternal Flame is inspecting this cave for heresy. He has a checklist. He has reached 'hydra' and is looking for a pencil.

outcome.text: He tasted of chalk and diligence. Someone will notice the inspections have stopped.
He wanders off, writing 'no hydra observed' with great confidence.

success.text: He ticks 'cave: damp' and leaves, satisfied with a job well done.

failure.text: He ticks 'hydra: yes' and blows a whistle. Two more novices arrive, both with torches.

events.title: A Certified Relic
events.text: A wooden box on a ledge, sealed with the Order's wax. The certificate inside swears it holds the left toe of Saint Cinder. It is the fourth left toe of Saint Cinder you have heard of.

outcome.text: It is, against all odds, a toe. Holy or not, it goes down well.
A pig's toe. The certificate, however, is perfectly genuine. The box is good for scrap.
Somewhere above, a pilgrimage is planned around this ledge. You have time.

events.title: Groaning Rock
events.text: The ceiling here creaks like an old man getting up. Small stones patter down. Something larger is thinking about it.

success.text: Nothing falls. The rock sighs behind you, disappointed.

failure.text: A boulder lands on the body. The heads argue about whose idea it was to hurry.

outcome.text: The ceiling settles. From the steady ledge you can see a good way down the tunnels.

events.title: The Drummer
events.text: A man sits in the dark, beating a drum made from his own shield. Every beat is slightly wrong. 'You hear it too,' he says. 'The song. It's out of tune. I am fixing it.' He is not fixing it.

success.text: For a moment the beats line up, and the heads hear something vast breathe in. The tunnels around you feel very clear.

failure.text: The wrong beat crawls into every skull at once. The heads spend the rest of the day arguing about rhythm.

outcome.text: The drum keeps going for a while on its own.
Behind you the beat goes on, wrong, and certain of itself.

events.title: Nine Candles
events.text: Nine unlit candles in a circle around a bowl of fish heads. A note in a shaky hand: 'For the Many-Headed. One candle for each head, when you have nine. We are patient.'

outcome.text: The heads count the candles, then each other. They arrive at different numbers.
Someone will come back and find it untouched. Somehow, that will mean a great deal to them.

events.title: A Warning in Chalk
events.text: Chalk on the wall: a serpent with one head, and next to it a hydra, crossed out nine times. Underneath, in capitals: THE SERPENT IS ONE. The chalk dust on the floor is fresh.

choices.text: Add a few heads to the serpent.

outcome.text: Better. The heads argue over whose likeness it is.
The chalk hisses off the wall, and a good deal of the wall goes with it. Underneath is softer, older rock.
You leave the wall as it is. It watches you go, with one eye.

events.title: A Warm Crack
events.text: The rock here is warm to the touch, and humming. Something inside is eating the heat, a little at a time, with many small mouths.

outcome.text: Warm, for the first time in a long time. The humming moves closer. You leave before it gets ideas, and take the warmth with you.
The humming stops. Then it starts again, further off, offended. The cooled rock cracks open onto a lookout.
Some doors are best left humming.

events.title: The Cinderkin
events.text: A swarm seeps out of a crack: insects of hot rock, each the size of a grain of rice and twice as hot. They circle you once, tasting the air, and settle on the wall to wait. They eat heat. They do not seem to mind where it comes from.

outcome.text: They find the warmth in your hide, and follow it into the rock like water into sand. Somewhere nearby, the rock begins to glow.
None of the heads can light a fire. You are a swamp. The Cinderkin light it themselves, eat it, and go looking for seconds. Somewhere nearby, the rock begins to glow.
Hot. Very hot. The Biter announces that it meant to do that. The swarm leaves, offended.
A thousand tiny glowing eyes watch you go, then go back to watching the rock.

events.title: The Tithe Box
events.text: An iron box bolted to the rock. On its lid: TITHES FOR THE ETERNAL FLAME. TEN PARTS IN A HUNDRED. RECEIPTS ISSUED.

outcome.text: Inside: a small fortune in muck and a receipt book. The Order will want the book back.
A receipt slides out of a slot. It thanks you for your contribution to the burning of your swamp.

events.title: A Ring of Pale Caps
events.text: A perfect circle of pale mushrooms. Inside it the dust lies very still, and time seems to be holding its breath. Something on the far side of the air is looking back.

success.text: For one long moment the heads are a single body and agree on everything. Afterwards they argue about who agreed first. The mycelium keeps whispering.

failure.text: Too many songs at once. Something with too many eyes says something kind, and it is the worst thing the heads have ever heard.

outcome.text: It tastes of earth and of the colour green. Afterwards the heads hear things a long way off. Some of them are even there.
Wise. The ring looks almost disappointed.

events.title: A Lost Pilgrim
events.text: A pilgrim of the Order, lost for days. He has eaten his candles. He asks, very politely, which way is up.

outcome.text: He thanks you and leaves to tell everyone about the kind monster. Nobody will believe the kind part.
He thanks you and walks deeper. The Order will search for him in all the wrong places.
He was mostly candle.

events.title: A Pillar of Salt
events.text: A man made of salt, caught mid-step, holding a lantern made of salt. A plaque at his feet: BROTHER OSRIC, WHO WAS TOLD TO WAIT HERE. He is still waiting.

outcome.text: Salt. Very loyal salt. Your hide stiffens.
The hand comes off with the lantern. Brother Osric does not complain. He is still waiting.
Somebody should come back for him. Nobody will.

events.title: An Old Skull
events.text: A skull with too many eye sockets, half sunk in the mud. Not human. Not quite yours. The teeth match your own.

outcome.text: None of the heads knows the words, so they hum something instead. For a moment it sounds like someone else's song.
Old marrow, dry as paper. Nobody says anything for a while. That night the necks ache, and in the morning they are thicker.

events.title: An Old Wallow
events.text: A hollow of mud so old it has gone black and soft as velvet. Something large wallowed here for a very long time, and left its smell behind as a kind of will.

outcome.text: The smell soaks in past the scales and stays. The heads complain about it, then stop noticing, which is worse.
Good mud. Old mud. It keeps its shape in the jaw.
Someone else's smell is someone else's business.

events.title: A Vein of Strange Salt
events.text: A vein of salt that glitters blue-green, licked smooth by something with a very long tongue. A sign of the Order: DO NOT LICK. Beneath it, in another hand: WE KNOW.

success.text: The salt tingles down the spine, and the spine stretches to follow it. There is more of you now, at both ends.

failure.text: The salt bites back. Every tongue goes numb, and the heads take turns blaming each other's.

outcome.text: DO NOT LICK. WE KNOW. The heads feel known.
Somebody has to obey the signs. Today it is you.

events.title: An Empty Egg
events.text: Half an eggshell, big as a cauldron, with the smell of your own kind still on it. Something hatched here long ago and left without cleaning up.

outcome.text: It goes down in pieces. Later the heads swear they can hear another one, very small, waiting its turn.
It still fits, more or less. Everyone sleeps better for it.
Whoever it was, they are not coming back for it.

events.title: A Carving in the Rock
events.text: Carved into the wall: tall figures, or long ones, it is hard to say, standing around a coiled shape. Their mouths are open. Beneath them run rows of marks like notes of music. Or teeth.

outcome.text: Each head reads the marks differently. One hears a lullaby, one a warning, one a shopping list. They agree it is important.

choices.text: Copy the marks onto a scale.

outcome.text: A precise copy, etched into a scale. A little itchy. The marks seem to point somewhere further in.
Old scratches on an old wall. The underground is full of them.

events.title: The Cold Machine
events.text: A machine of brass pipes and stone bellows, taller than the hydra, grown over with moss. Pipes run down into the rock, toward something warm. The coiled shape from the carving is hammered into its side. It is silent, but only just.

outcome.text: The pipes cough mist, then hold one low note. Far below, something turns over in its sleep.

success.text: It shudders and hums a single note. Then it sulks. Far below, something stirs.

failure.text: A pipe bursts. Scalding steam, and an echo that carries a long way.

outcome.text: Good metal. The machine lets out a long, thin whistle as it comes apart, like someone remembering a tune too late.

events.title: The Last Note
events.text: A round chamber with walls too smooth for any tool. In the middle lies a mask with no mouth, made for a face longer than any human's. As you come near, the whole room hums the note the machine played.

outcome.text: The note opens like a door. For one heartbeat you understand the song. Then the heartbeat ends, but the tunnels around stay clear in your mind.

choices.text: Take the mask to Old Mother Toad.

outcome.text: It weighs nothing. The heads take turns carrying it, and none of them wants a turn.
It tastes of nothing at all. The humming stops. Everyone pretends not to be relieved.

events.title: A Surveyor's Stake
events.text: A red-painted stake, a measuring chain, and a sign: THIS CAVE IS THE PROPERTY OF THE ORDER OF THE ETERNAL FLAME, PENDING SURVEY. TRESPASSERS WILL BE CATALOGUED.

outcome.text: The chain runs off into the dark, marked every ten yards in neat red paint.

choices.text: Move the stake a few yards.

outcome.text: According to the Order, this cave is now slightly smaller.
It tastes of red paint and good intentions.

events.title: The Surveyors
events.text: Three surveyors of the Order sit round a lantern, arguing over a map. The map is upside down. One of them sees you and writes something down.

outcome.text: The surveyors drop the map and pick up torches. Two of them, anyway. The third keeps writing.

success.text: They measure every neck, twice. The report will call you 'a large damp nuisance, not a priority'.

failure.text: They measure every neck, twice, and then they count the necks. They count again. One of them runs.

outcome.text: The Acid Spitter cannot bear an upside-down map. It turns it the right way up, then makes a few improvements. The surveyors leave to chart a lake that is not there.

events.title: The Survey Office
events.text: A camp table in the dark: ink, wax, the seal of the Order and a stack of forms. A sign on the table: SUBTERRANEAN SURVEY OFFICE. CLOSED FOR PRAYER.

outcome.text: Officially, this hydra has been seen to. It says so in red wax.
Neat, careful maps, every one of them wrong in a different and useful way.
The Order will have to fill them all in again. It is the cruellest thing you have ever done.

events.//: M4: events on the surface name its biome (conditions.biomes); the others happen only underground.
events.title: A Scarecrow in a Tabard
events.text: In the middle of a field stands a scarecrow in the tabard of the Order. Someone has painted on a stern face. The crows have not been told.

outcome.text: Straw and a tabard. The heads agree it was the most honest member of the Order they have met.

choices.text: Put its hat on The Spare.

outcome.text: The Spare wears it all day. A patrol passes at a distance and salutes.
It keeps watch over the field. It has never caught anything, and it is not about to start.

events.title: The Village Well
events.text: A well at the edge of a village, a bucket on a rope, and a sign: BLESSED BY THE ORDER. DO NOT SPIT.

outcome.text: The heads drink in turns, then all at once. The village will want to know where its water went.
The Acid Spitter reads the sign twice, then spits. The Order will have to come and bless it all over again, and it has better things to do.
You leave it. The sign seems disappointed.

events.title: Pilgrims on the Road
events.text: Three pilgrims walk to a Flame Shrine with lanterns and a hymn. They have not seen you. The hymn has a verse about you, and it is not flattering.

outcome.text: The hymn stops in the middle of the verse. The shrine will wait for its pilgrims a long time.
They walk into the mist and come out at the river, lanterns out. They agree it was a sign.

success.text: The heads hum the tune. The pilgrims hurry on, and swear afterwards that the hills were singing.

failure.text: One head sings the words. The pilgrims drop their lanterns and run for the castle.

events.title: A Field
events.text: A ploughed field under the open sky. Nothing happens here, which up here is called farming.

outcome.text: Warm earth. The heads lie very still and pretend to be a hedge.
Turnips, mostly. And worms, which are better.

events.title: A Still Pool
events.text: A still, black pool. Nothing happens here, which in the underground counts as an event.

outcome.text: Cold, clean, and quiet.
The heads doze off one by one. None at the same time, but it's a start.
